package_info.package_versions: All versions prior to patched Google Camera/Samsung Camera apps (pre-July 2019)
package_info.why_malicious: The package abuses Android camera app intent handling to bypass camera and microphone permissions, allowing a rogue app to take photos, record video/audio, and exfiltrate sensitive data (including GPS metadata) without user consent. It also maintains persistent C&C communication for remote exploitation.

execution_context.file_location: malicious app main activity / background service

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends a crafted intent to the camera app to take a photo, stores the image in accessible storage, and uploads it to a remote C&C server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app triggers the camera to take photos without user interaction or camera permission.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps require explicit user consent and camera permissions to access the camera; this app bypasses those controls.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate camera apps or automation tools may use similar intents, but only with user consent and proper permissions.
key_indicators: Camera triggered via intent from background app
Automatic upload of captured image to remote server

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on C&C command or proximity sensor event)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends a crafted intent to the camera app to record video (including audio), stores the video in accessible storage, and uploads it to a remote C&C server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app records video and audio without user knowledge or camera/microphone permissions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps require explicit user consent and permissions for video/audio recording; this app circumvents those requirements.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate automation or security apps may record video, but only with user awareness and permission.
key_indicators: Video recording triggered by background app
Automatic upload of video to remote server

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After capturing a photo, the code parses EXIF metadata for GPS coordinates and uploads the location data to a remote C&C server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app extracts and exfiltrates sensitive location data without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps do not access or transmit location metadata from photos without explicit user permission.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Photo management apps may read EXIF data for sorting or mapping, but not for covert exfiltration.
key_indicators: Automated EXIF parsing for GPS data

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on C&C command or proximity sensor event)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code monitors the proximity sensor to detect a voice call, then triggers video and audio recording to capture both sides of the conversation, uploading the result to a remote C&C server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app covertly records private conversations without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps do not record calls or use sensors to trigger covert recording without explicit user approval.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Call recording apps exist, but require explicit user permission and legal compliance.
key_indicators: Proximity sensor used to trigger recording

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On app startup, the code establishes a persistent connection to a remote C&C server, allowing remote attackers to issue commands for photo, video, and audio capture.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app maintains a stealthy, persistent connection to an external server for remote control.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps do not maintain persistent C&C connections for remote exploitation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate apps use persistent connections for notifications, but not for remote device control.

attack_chain.action: Malicious app is installed and establishes a persistent connection to the attacker's C&C server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote attacker can issue commands to the device.

attack_chain.action: Attacker issues command to take a photo, record video, or record audio (including during calls).
attack_chain.leads_to: Device captures sensitive media without user knowledge.

attack_chain.action: Captured photos and videos are stored in accessible storage; app parses EXIF data for GPS location.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive media and location data are ready for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: App uploads captured media and extracted GPS/location data to the attacker's C&C server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to private photos, videos, audio, and location data.

behavioral_signatures: Background apps sending camera/video capture intents without camera permission
Apps accessing and parsing EXIF GPS metadata from photos without user interaction
Persistent outbound connections to unknown servers from non-network-centric apps
Media capture triggered by proximity sensor events
file_indicators: Unexpected photos/videos appearing in camera roll
App accessing camera/media storage without user-initiated action
Frequent access to EXIF data in app logs
network_indicators: Outbound connections to C&C infrastructure (unknown IPs/domains)
Uploads of media files (photos/videos/audio) to remote servers
Persistent TCP connections from background services
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for apps that trigger camera or video capture intents without holding camera/microphone permissions, especially if they only request storage permission. Flag apps that access EXIF GPS metadata or upload media files to external servers. Use network monitoring to detect persistent outbound connections from apps not expected to maintain such connections. Alert on media capture events triggered by background services or proximity sensor events.
